Hi everyone, and welcome. A few practical things before tonight. The welcome dinner starts at seven, and it is not optional. If you are tired, come anyway and leave early. Nobody will notice when you leave, but everybody will notice if you are not there. Tomorrow, orientation starts at eight thirty in the main hall. If you are late, do not walk to the front. Sit in the back, and we will find you at the break. Your study group is on the back of your name tag. If you lose the tag, the front desk will print a new one. And one more thing. If you have a question, ask it. This week is expensive, and the questions are the cheapest part of it.

The first time a professor cold called me, I was sure my English would fail. She said my name and asked one question: would you sell the company? I had two seconds. I said, no, because the market will recover next year. That was it. One sentence and one reason. Here is what I learned that morning. If you try to give a perfect answer, you will freeze. If you give a short answer, the professor will ask a follow-up question, and then you are in a conversation, not in an exam. On Monday I was afraid of the cold call. By Wednesday I wanted it. By Friday I was raising my hand.
